📄 NUET Math Specification 🌙

This is the official specification file for NUET Math.

Use it to check the exam content, structure and general scope of the syllabus.

🌙 Direct and Inverse Proportion

In this topic, you need to understand how two quantities are related. In direct proportion, both quantities change in the same direction. In inverse proportion, when one quantity increases, the other decreases.

You should be able to:
• identify whether the relationship is direct or inverse
• set up a proportion from a table or a word problem
• find missing values correctly
• solve practical questions involving cost, work, time, speed or quantity

Pay close attention to wording, because exam questions often hide the proportion inside a real-life situation.

No extra files have been added for this topic yet.

🌙 Recurring Decimals

This topic is about decimals in which one digit or a block of digits repeats forever. You need to understand the notation and convert recurring decimals into fractions.

You should revise:
• how to identify the repeating part
• notation for recurring decimals
• converting simple recurring decimals into fractions
• converting mixed recurring decimals into fractions

This topic is mainly about method, so make sure you understand each algebraic step clearly.

No extra files have been added for this topic yet.

🌙 Algebraic Simplification

This topic checks whether you can work accurately with algebraic expressions. You need to simplify expressions step by step and avoid combining terms incorrectly.

You should revise:
• collecting like terms
• expanding brackets
• factorising simple expressions
• simplifying algebraic fractions when possible
• handling expressions with x carefully

A common mistake is combining unlike terms, so always check that the variables and powers match.

No extra files have been added for this topic yet.

🌙 Circle Theorems

This is one of the most important geometry topics. You need to know the standard circle theorems and use them correctly in diagrams.

You should revise:
• angle at the center and angle at the circumference
• angles in the same segment
• angle in a semicircle
• cyclic quadrilateral theorem
• tangent and radius relationships
• chord properties and intersecting chords

Do not revise this topic only by reading theory. Practice with diagrams, because the exam usually tests recognition of the correct theorem.

No extra files have been added for this topic yet.

🌙 Percentages Word Problems

This topic focuses on using percentages in practical situations such as discounts, increase, decrease, profit and original price questions.

You should revise:
• finding a percentage of a quantity
• percentage increase and decrease
• finding the new value after change
• finding the original value
• interpreting wording carefully in real-life questions

A common mistake is using the wrong base value, so always check which number the percentage refers to.

No extra files have been added for this topic yet.

🌙 Rounding and Standard Form

This topic tests your accuracy with very large and very small numbers. You should know how to round correctly and how to write numbers in standard form.

You should revise:
• significant figures
• difference between decimal places and significant figures
• writing numbers in standard form
• converting standard form back to ordinary form
• simple calculations with numbers in standard form

Read the instruction carefully, because many mistakes happen when students confuse decimal places and significant figures.

No extra files have been added for this topic yet.

🌙 Graph Transformation

This topic is about understanding how a graph changes when the equation changes. You should connect the algebraic form of a function with the movement of the graph.

You should revise:
• translations up, down, left and right
• reflections in the x-axis and y-axis
• stretches and compressions
• transformations of parabolas and basic functions

Try to understand the meaning of each change instead of memorizing rules mechanically.

No extra files have been added for this topic yet.

🌙 Vertex / Turning Point of a Parabola

This topic focuses on quadratic graphs. You need to identify the turning point, understand the axis of symmetry and connect the equation with the shape of the graph.

You should revise:
• finding the turning point from a graph
• understanding vertex form
• axis of symmetry
• maximum and minimum values
• sketching a quadratic graph correctly

This topic often appears together with graph interpretation and quadratic equations.

No extra files have been added for this topic yet.

🌙 Vectors

Vectors describe movement with both magnitude and direction. You should be able to use vector notation and solve geometric problems involving vectors.

You should revise:
• vector notation
• addition and subtraction of vectors
• multiplying a vector by a scalar
• magnitude of a vector
• vector problems in geometry

Work step by step and keep track of direction carefully.

No extra files have been added for this topic yet.

🌙 Bearings

This topic deals with direction measured clockwise from north. You need to read, draw and use three-figure bearings correctly.

You should revise:
• what a bearing means
• measuring clockwise from north
• writing bearings as three-figure angles
• drawing bearings accurately
• solving direction and distance problems

A common mistake is measuring from the wrong starting line, so always begin from north.

No extra files have been added for this topic yet.

🌙 Parallel and Perpendicular Lines

This topic connects straight-line equations with geometric properties. You should understand how gradients show whether lines are parallel or perpendicular.

You should revise:
• gradient of a line
• condition for parallel lines
• condition for perpendicular lines
• equations of straight lines
• finding an unknown line from given conditions

Remember that parallel lines have equal gradients, while perpendicular lines have gradients related by negative reciprocal values.

No extra files have been added for this topic yet.

🌙 Coordinate Geometry

This topic involves solving geometric problems using coordinates and formulas. You should connect points, lines and distance with algebraic methods.

You should revise:
• midpoint formula
• distance formula
• gradient formula
• equation of a line
• interpreting the geometry behind coordinate calculations

Practice full questions, because coordinate geometry often combines several formulas in one problem.

No extra files have been added for this topic yet.

🌙 Rhombus, Kite and Trapezium

This topic is about the properties of common quadrilaterals. You need to recognize their side, angle, diagonal and symmetry properties.

You should revise:
• properties of a rhombus
• properties of a kite
• properties of a trapezium
• diagonals and angle relationships
• area and perimeter when relevant

Questions may ask you to identify a shape from its properties, not only from its name.

No extra files have been added for this topic yet.

🌙 Trigonometry in Right-Angled Triangles

This is a core topic in geometry. You need to use sine, cosine and tangent to find missing sides and angles.

You should revise:
• SOH CAH TOA
• opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse
• finding a missing side
• finding a missing angle
• applied problems using right-angled triangles

The main difficulty is choosing the correct ratio, so always label the triangle first.

No extra files have been added for this topic yet.

🌙 Exponents with Bases 2, 3 and 5

This topic tests whether you understand the laws of indices and can rewrite expressions using the same base.

You should revise:
• multiplication and division of powers
• power of a power
• zero and negative powers where relevant
• rewriting numbers using bases 2, 3 and 5
• simplifying exponential expressions step by step

Focus on the laws of indices rather than memorizing isolated tricks.

No extra files have been added for this topic yet.

🌙 Real-life Graphs, Especially Velocity-Time

This topic tests whether you understand what a graph means in a real situation. It is not only about shape, but also about interpretation.

You should revise:
• distance-time graphs
• velocity-time graphs
• meaning of gradient
• meaning of area under a velocity-time graph
• comparing motion across different parts of a graph

Be careful not to confuse distance-time graphs with velocity-time graphs.

No extra files have been added for this topic yet.

🌙 Compound 3D Figures

This topic involves solids made from more than one 3D shape. You need to break the figure into parts and apply formulas correctly.

You should revise:
• volume of a cylinder, cone and sphere
• surface area where relevant
• splitting a solid into simpler parts
• adding or subtracting volumes
• checking units carefully

These questions are often more about structure than memorization, so first decide what shapes are present.
